statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the sum of the values v of all nodes of root whose value v satisfies low <= v <= high. Each such node contributes its value exactly once, and no node outside the inclusive interval [low, high] contributes.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail with overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds on any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high <= 100000.

statement: Let k be the number of nodes of root whose value v satisfies low <= v <= high. The function returns a result r, and k * low <= r <= k * high.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high <= 100000.

statement: Let r1 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low1, high1) and r2 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low2, high2). The function returns both results, and r2 <= r1.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low1 <= low2 <= high2 <= high1 <= 100000.

statement: Let r1 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low, high) and r2 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low, high + 1). The function returns both results, and r2 = r1 + (high + 1) if some node of root has value high + 1, and r2 = r1 otherwise.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high < 100000.

statement: Let r1 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low, high) and r2 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low - 1, high). The function returns both results, and r2 = r1 + (low - 1) if some node of root has value low - 1, and r2 = r1 otherwise.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 < low <= high <= 100000.

statement: For every integer mid with low <= mid < high, let r be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low, high), let r1 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, low, mid), and let r2 be the result of range_sum_bst(root, mid + 1, high). The function returns these results, and r = r1 + r2.
preconditions: The tree root is a nonempty binary search tree with at most 20000 nodes; every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are distinct; for every node, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high <= 100000.

statement: Let r1 be the result of range_sum_bst(root1, low, high) and r2 be the result of range_sum_bst(root2, low, high). The function returns both results, and r1 = r2.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are each nonempty binary search trees with at most 20000 nodes; every node value in either tree is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values within each tree are distinct; for every node in either tree, all values in its left subtree are less than its value and all values in its right subtree are greater than its value; 1 <= low <= high <= 100000; the set of values v of nodes of root1 with low <= v <= high equals the set of values v of nodes of root2 with low <= v <= high.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r > 0 if and only if there exists at least one node of root whose value v satisfies low <= v <= high.

statement: For every node of root whose value v satisfies low <= v <= high, the returned result r satisfies r >= v.
